[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/11540/diffs?diff_id=746108795&start_sha=4cc13c61804715885672e0545d88ccdd2017a045)

It is not a good idea to put UI stuff into the constructor. Better keep it in the UI dialog itself, as it allows for better restyling of dialogs.

Also, we do not use "auto" generally throughout the code. I know it is a nuisance, but it makes for better readable code.

Please use the monospace font set by the user

changed this line in [version 3 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/11540/diffs?diff_id=747360663&start_sha=82bdd7a5b64b65b8e8f40fc8b9e09930a85353fd#9274b313c21144d96ef72aa3661b5856238709ba_30_32)

This creates 4 copies of String before the final result. It is fine here, but .arg in general should be avoided, at least if it is to be concatenated. .append does not do copy

changed this line in [version 3 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/11540/diffs?diff_id=747360663&start_sha=82bdd7a5b64b65b8e8f40fc8b9e09930a85353fd#9274b313c21144d96ef72aa3661b5856238709ba_55_124)
OK
So, this error message would stand, even if you are already looking for a new Mac address?

This is a textual output and everything stands until the user clicks "Clear".

Naturally other designs can be considered but this seems OK for a first approach.

It's simple for sure, I don't claim to be a GUI design whizz. :slight_smile:

This would deviate from all our user concepts and should be avoided. Usually our dialogs are self-resetting, which is easy enough done in this case. Just add a slot onTextChanged, check if an error is set and reset the output message.

If the only method for the clear button really remains to clear the output message, I would consider this an issue that needs to be fixed.

There isn't a single message, there are many. It's useful to keep the history. It's emulating a console and it's working more or less like a console would. I don't really see an issue. 

It's not clear to me what you are proposing. It should clear the TextEdit with every search or just with errors or ...?
To be quite honest, I have not compiled the patch yet, just went from source code. I will do that now and get back to you

Ok, I See where you were going with that, and for that it is clear. The overall mission of the dialog becomes less so.

Consider the following screen: ![image](/uploads/372438b6e70a0786c3dfb6eb4b9786e3/image.png)

You could argue, that entering only two bytes of a MAC address is not a valid Mac address. But you are also not making an address lookup, but rather an OUI-24 (the vendor part of a Mac address) lookup. Which is what I expected going into the dialog, but at the same time it does not state so in the title and the text for the Combobox.

Furthermore, just entering two bytes results in only a single result, but not necessarily the one I am looking for, which can lead to issues. Why was that selected (my guess would be because it is alphabetically the first) and not the other? You have to work with the user expectation here. That would be, that it would return all addresses that start with that byte sequence.

A different thing is the name lookup. Most of the vendor ID lookup sites work both ways. You can either search for the vendor ID or the vendor name. In the case of this dialog, only the full vendor ID will lead to valid results, everything else leads to an error.

Initially I only intended to work with full MAC addresses but then I realized it would return results with MAC slices and I just left it like that. But you are right, it should use a proper address mask.

The vendor lookup is future work too.

changed this line in [version 3 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/11540/diffs?diff_id=747360663&start_sha=82bdd7a5b64b65b8e8f40fc8b9e09930a85353fd#9274b313c21144d96ef72aa3661b5856238709ba_67_142)
The prefix is zero-filled. Other than the fact that I was using the name "MAC Lookup" instead of OUI seems OK actually.
Personally I like the idea of this tool, just so you know ;-)

I think it would be useful if the search results could be copied.
I agree. The multi-cell copying works very well with the Authors table. I assumed this was a feature of QTableView but it's not, apparently, so I will have to try and find time to add that.

Sorry @jvalverde I couldn't get back due to a family emergency. It still leads to wrong results (aka "00:00" does not list all possibilities) and it is still misleading in naming. Also, the model is implemented wrongly. Models should always load all possible information (or provide a lazy-search interface) not being populated when something is found. In such a case a QTableWidget would have been a better choice, although we are trying to avoid those.

I know that this does not fit then further with the way you are trying to load via the epan-interface, but here you are breaking Qt guidelines, which is not a good thing either. Additionally, if the model would load everything, you could easily let it search for regular expressions as well as do not have to distinguish between strings or numerals.

I also agree on the copy part, but that can be done in a separate commit.

Personally, I would not have merged it right now, as it still feels "unfinished".

No problem, let's keep the discussion going.

> It still leads to wrong results (aka "00:00" does not list all possibilities) and it is still misleading in naming.

The way it is working is that it zero-extends the input bytes to create a 6-byte MAC address. So I think it is correct, it's just lax in how it accepts input for convenience sake.

> Also, the model is implemented wrongly. Models should always load all possible information (or provide a lazy-search interface) not being populated when something is found. In such a case a QTableWidget would have been a better choice, although we are trying to avoid those.

I will look up the Qt guidelines, thanks for the pointer.

I'm not against doing that, I think showing all the information and filtering is an elegant solution, but I ran out of time to work on it and IMHO it's already useful and good enough to release as is.

> The way it is working is that it zero-extends the input bytes to create a 6-byte MAC address. So I think it is correct, it's just lax in how it accepts input for convenience sake.

The issue with this is, that the user will not guess this. It might be working in the sense that it reaches results, but from an UX experience it is not working correctly. I get the way you extend it, but this leads to issues as said before.

Better would be, to load all the vendor codes and then let a ProxyModel regex-search over it. It will add load-time though.

> The issue with this is, that the user will not guess this. It might be working in the sense that it reaches results, but from an UX experience it is not working correctly. I get the way you extend it, but this leads to issues as said before.

That's why I added a hint with the full matched address, because it's not obvious how it is transforming the input, inlcuding the masked bits. It's still lacking documentation and tooltips though.

commits_data.message:
GUI: Implement Tools->MAC Address Blocks menu entry

Add a dialog to lookup a MAC address or vendor name in the\
internal IEEE manufacturer registry.
